prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Context: Meridian region dense aviation area (hub, domestic, cargo/GA aerodromes sharing terminal airspace); twice-daily peaks; near capacity in Normal Operations (mode). Constraints: shared fixes, weather lowering Airport Acceptance Rate, military/special-use airspace, surface limits. Mission: resilient, governed, interoperable ATFM and Airport Collaborative Decision-Making (A-CDM) reducing avoidable delay, improving predictability. Airports: Meridian International, Harbor East, North Valley, Lakeside Regional, Southport; each keeps local safety management, certification, command authority. System-of-interest: Regional Flow Platform (alias Cedarbell), a shared coordination layer; does not replace statutory ATC, airport control rooms, airline operational control centers, ground handling dispatch. Parts: planning/assessment: Demand Prediction Service (demand from schedules, Flight Intent Message, airline recovery plans), Capacity Assessment Module (capacity from weather, runways, sector loading, resources), Slot Allocation Engine (fair traceable allocation), Airport CDM Portal (readiness sharing, surface/terminal decisions), Digital Briefing Room. Tactical: Tower Sequence Manager, Ramp Movement Board, Departure Metering Service, Arrival Regulation Console, Contingency Operations Console. Integration: Weather Ingest Gateway, Flight Data Exchange, Surface Surveillance Adapter, Airline Interface Adapter, Alert Distribution Hub. Governance: Performance Analytics Warehouse, Audit Event Ledger, Identity Access Service, Business Rules Registry, Time Synchronization Service, Collaborative Decision Log (rationale, timing, authorization). Connected components: North/South Runway Meter, East/West Apron Sensor, Sector Load Monitor, Gate Conflict Detector. Common Situation Display shows demand, capacity, constraints, measures to authorized users. External (outside): airline reservation, crew management, baggage reconciliation, airport commercial systems, national surveillance, aircraft avionics; interfaces only for identity validation, receiving authorized data, publishing approved coordination info, audit records. Actors: Regional Flow Manager (primary, regional demand/capacity balance); Airline Operations Coordinator, Network Operations Liaison, Aircraft Operator Representative, Slot Coordinator; Tower Supervisor, Ramp Control Lead, Airport Duty Manager, Ground Handling Dispatcher, Deicing Coordinator; Meteorology Briefing Officer, Airspace Sector Planner, Military Airspace Liaison, Emergency Response Coordinator; Data Governance Steward, System Support Engineer. Airlines: scheduled passenger, cargo, charter, based carriers. Ground providers: handlers, fueling, deicing, towing, passenger transport, ramp services (airport-approved). Modes/requirements: Adverse Weather Mode or Capacity Reduction State: must support rapid

New part:
S045: Air navigation service participation includes regional flow management personnel, tower supervisory personnel, airspace planning personnel, and any designated military coordination function that affects civil capacity planning.
S046: The shared operational picture includes Flight Intent Message status, Airport Capacity Plan assumptions, Target Off Block Time values, Calculated Takeoff Time values, Airport Acceptance Rate constraints, Common Situation Display content, Tactical Regulation Proposal status, Collaborative Decision Log entries, and Post Operations Report outputs.
S047: The system boundary explicitly covers Normal Operations, Adverse Weather Mode, Capacity Reduction State, Recovery Phase, Contingency Fallback State, and Slot Compliance State because these states drive stakeholder participation and operating procedures.
S048: Participation in the regional system requires each stakeholder organization to assign accountable representatives, maintain current contact details, follow agreed data use rules, and support post-operational review of decisions made through the Regional Flow Platform.
S049: The daily planning cycle begins with a pre-tactical baseline prepared each morning before the main bank structure is locked for operational use.
S050: The Regional Flow Manager owns the baseline process and confirms that the planning horizon, cutover time, and review checkpoints are understood by the participating operational roles.
S051: The Regional Flow Platform creates the initial demand picture from published schedules, approved seasonal allocations, overnight schedule changes, and received Flight Intent Message data.
S052: The Flight Data Exchange normalizes flight identifiers, aircraft types, routing fields, and planned operating times so that later comparisons use a single reference record.
S053: The Demand Prediction Service converts the normalized schedule into expected arrival and departure demand by time band, runway direction, terminal area, and major traffic flow.
S054: The Airline Operations Coordinator reviews material deviations from filed intent, including aircraft swaps, early cancellations, recovery flights, and known connection protection actions.
S055: The Aircraft Operator Representative validates that operator priorities are visible where they are allowed by the Business Rules Registry and local coordination agreements.
S056: The Meteorology Briefing Officer provides the morning weather outlook with emphasis on wind trend, ceiling, visibility, convective risk, temperature limits, and confidence over the planning horizon.
S057: The Weather Ingest Gateway makes the outlook available to the Capacity Assessment Module and preserves the forecast issue time for audit and later performance review.
S058: The Airspace Sector Planner declares expected sector constraints, route availability assumptions, and any planned staffing limitations that could influence arrival or departure metering.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
